blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Psychological Association of the Philippines (PAP) on Monday called for a law that protects children from online dangers while preserving opportunities for learning and connection. PAP said a blanket age-based prohibition “should not be the primary or stand-alone measure,” adding that “age thresholds have a place, but the evidence supports the specific features, interactions, and design choices through which harm occurs.” Evidence, it said in a statement, supports imposing enforceable duties on the platforms that control these features and building the support systems children need when harm occurs.
